1.9 Verify a completed receiver without replaying its initial transfer

Prerequisites. Retain the accepted native transfer result, its source and destination scope, original direction policy, adopted owner record and declared preview aliases. Distinguish that historical acceptance from current state.

Mechanism. An initial receiver may force one source toward its destination. After takeover, the destination can contain newer catalog edits and newly built previews. Repeating the forced profile is a write operation, not a coherence check. Native discovery-cache reuse does not make that direction safe.

Verify. Authenticate the saved acceptance and owner-adoption controls. At an authorized owned boundary, compare the current owner, exact alias targets and expected volume/directory identities, then verify the current catalog launch, application version and required startup phases. Keep later generated previews and any subsequent synchronization direction in a separate reviewed scope. Reusing the saved native assurance does not prove current whole-tree equality.

Undo and limits. This verification does not change data or transfer authority. On a mismatch, retain evidence and stop before synchronization. Do not rerun an old forced profile, overwrite a newer catalog, or rehash/recopy the whole cache merely to repeat an already accepted receiver. A changed source or conflicting scope needs a new direction and preservation review. Server convergence remains a separate native observation.
